corrugate-vs-five.title: Corrugated vs five-rib roofing: what changes the choice?
corrugate-vs-five.description: Compare NZ corrugated and five-rib roof profiles, minimum pitches, cover widths, installation scope and material pricing without confusing profile with coating.
corrugate-vs-five.answer: Corrugate and five-rib are shapes, not competing steel brands. Choose the exact profile for your roof pitch and design first, then compare the same metal, coating, thickness and installed scope. Neither shape is universally cheaper, and a per-metre sheet price is not a finished-roof price.

sections.title: What is actually different?

blocks.caption: Corrugated and five-rib roofing comparison

cells: Raised angular ribs with flatter pans
What to compare on a quote
Named profile, metal, coating, thickness and accessories

blocks.text: Published minima are product starting points, not approval for your roof. Sheet length, drainage, wind design and installation details still need checking against the current manufacturer manual.

Think of the specification as four separate decisions: shape, base metal, protective coating and installed system. Asking only for “COLORSTEEL” does not identify the shape; asking only for “five-rib” does not identify its coating or gauge. A useful quote names all four.

sections.title: Which NZ product names mean five-rib?

blocks.text: Metalcraft MC760 and T-Rib are trapezoidal choices. Dimond calls its five-rib profile Hi Five. Similar-looking profiles are not interchangeable order codes. Confirm the local branch, exact cover and matching ridge, hip and valley details.

A useful source check: Dimond’s Hi Five page currently shows 765 mm cover in its overview and 755 mm in its performance section. We have not silently selected one. Ask Dimond to confirm the current ordering width before using it for a takeoff.

blocks.title: Need the full NZ profile comparison?
blocks.text: Compare eight profile entries, supplier listings and project accounts with their source conditions.
blocks.label: Open the five-rib reference guide

sections.title: Does five-rib cost more?

blocks.text: One public retail listing offers both steel profiles at $17.49 per lineal metre including GST. It describes 0.5 mm gauge steel but does not establish that it is the same specification as a locally quoted branded roof. This is a material listing, not installation evidence.

On the same effective cover, an identical lineal price produces an identical sheet-area cost. Where covers differ, compare price divided by effective cover in metres. Do not use the overall sheet width, because side laps would then be counted as usable roof.

The arithmetic shows why a material ranking should not be forced to match an expected installed ranking. It says nothing about whether these two hypothetical sheets have equivalent coatings, warranties or structural performance.

sections.title: Where can the installed difference come from?

blocks.text: Do not assume all five-rib ridges must be hand-notched. NZMRM includes soft-edge treatment for low trapezoidal profiles, and Trimrib has both soft-edge and scribed/notched ridge drawings. Compare the actual specified detail.

Installation differences should be explained in the quote rather than assumed from a profile name. Ask whether angled cuts and profile-matched ridge and hip work change the labour on your particular roof. The useful comparison is the finished scope, not a universal five-rib surcharge.

Ask the roofer where the additional work is priced. If cut sheets, notched flashings and complex junctions are already priced as separate components, adding another blanket “complex roof” allowance for the same tasks can double-count them.

items: Compare the same roof area and the same plan-versus-slope basis.
List ridge, hip, valley and barge lengths separately.
Confirm underlay, fixings, delivery and wastage.
Separate old-roof removal and access from the new covering.

sections.title: What do real projects tell us?

blocks.text: These two jobs illustrate design constraints and scope. Neither publisher supplies enough cost and area information to calculate a defensible price difference between profiles.

sections.title: What should you ask for next?

blocks.text: For an existing roof, start with its pitch, condition and junctions. For a new design, compare the desired appearance alongside drainage and support requirements. Then request two like-for-like specifications rather than two vague “metal roof” totals.

items: Write down the exact manufacturer and profile.
Ask for base metal thickness and coating name, not just colour.
Confirm suitability for the site and the roof’s lowest-pitch section.
Ask the contractor to explain any difference in labour or accessory cost.

faqs.q: Is five-rib the same as COLORSTEEL?
faqs.a: No. Five-rib describes a profile family. COLORSTEEL names a material range; the exact profile and coating product still need to be specified.

cost-200.title: How much does a 200m² roof cost in New Zealand?
cost-200.description: Work through 200m² roof cost examples with explicit area, GST, source dates, new-roof versus reroof scope and a calculator for your own quoted rates.
cost-200.answer: First establish whether 200m² means sloping roof surface, horizontal roof projection or total house floor area. Those are different quantities. For a 200m² sloping roof, a hypothetical $150–$200/m² rate gives $30,000–$40,000 on that rate’s stated GST and scope basis. This is arithmetic, not a RoofHub market quote.

sections.title: Is your 200m² figure the right area?

blocks.caption: Three different meanings of 200 square metres

cells: Use 200m² for covering and removal before any separate order allowance.
Horizontal projection of the roof, including eaves
Convert each roof plane using its pitch.
Treating it as sloping surface area.
Establish the footprint and roof geometry first.
Using both storeys as roof area.

blocks.text: For a single-pitch 200m² roof projection at 25°, surface area is 200 ÷ cos(25°) = 220.7m². At a hypothetical $150–$200/m², that changes the covering-related total to about $33,100–$44,100. If the starting figure excludes eaves, add their projected area before the conversion.

sections.title: What do different quoted rates produce?

blocks.caption: RoofHub arithmetic examples, not current market offers

blocks.text: All rows inherit the input rate’s GST and inclusions. These are hypothetical rates, not a prediction that a particular roof system can be bought at that price. Use an actual written rate for a meaningful comparison.

sections.title: How do published NZ prices help?

blocks.text: The whole-job observations do not state that every roof is exactly 200m². Do not divide their endpoints by 200 and call the result a measured square-metre rate. The historical per-m² example can be scaled only on an explicitly assumed compatible area basis.

A good comparison keeps three layers apart: what the source actually published, any RoofHub arithmetic derived from it, and the supplier’s current written offer. A review date confirms that a page was checked; it does not make a 2025 rate a 2026 quote.

sections.title: What belongs in the total?

items: New covering, matching flashings and fasteners.
Underlay and any required substrate or batten work.
Removal, transport and disposal for a reroof.
Site safety/access and the included hire period.
Gutters, downpipes, insulation or repairs only where expressly included.
GST shown on the complete total, with exclusions listed.

blocks.text: Compare inclusions line by line before comparing the final number. A quote with scaffold already included should not receive the estimator’s scaffold allowance again. Likewise, do not add roof removal to a published complete-reroof rate that already includes it.

sections.title: Why can two 200m² roofs cost different amounts?

blocks.text: Area measures quantity, not all the work. Two roofs can share an area while one has much longer ridges, several valleys, restricted delivery access and more flashings. Record those quantities instead of assuming every difference can be explained by a flat percentage.
For a roof with unresolved substrate condition, ask for a written process for opening-up discoveries: what is included, what is a provisional allowance, and what requires approval as a variation.

sections.title: What information makes the estimate useful?

blocks.text: Bring a plan or measured roof area, material preference, existing roof type, storeys, pitch and access notes. The detailed estimator accepts component lengths as well as area. A contractor still needs to verify measurements and site conditions before issuing a quote.

faqs.q: Is the example a quote for my home?
faqs.a: No. It demonstrates area multiplied by a stated rate. Site conditions, scope, product and current prices must still be confirmed.

lifespan.title: How long does a metal roof last in New Zealand?
lifespan.description: Understand the difference between roof lifespan, product warranty and Building Code durability, with maintenance and reroof decision questions for NZ homes.
lifespan.answer: There is no single supported expiry age for every NZ metal roof. Actual service life depends on the product, exposure, detailing, maintenance and condition. A warranty term or Building Code durability requirement is not a prediction of how long your particular roof will remain serviceable.

sections.title: Which lifespan number are you looking at?

blocks.caption: Do not confuse these three measures

cells: Required performance period under the applicable conditions.
The roof needs replacement when that period ends.
A remedy for defined failures, subject to exclusions and maintenance.
Every component or every cause of a leak is covered.
Whether the installed assembly remains fit for use.
A fixed national average applying to all metal roofs.

blocks.text: The NZ Metal Roofing Manufacturers’ discussion of B2 describes the 15-year requirement for relevant accessible cladding applications and distinguishes it from longer durability requirements for some building elements. It should not be reworded as “metal roofs last 15 years”.

sections.title: What do current manufacturer examples show?

blocks.text: New Zealand Steel lists 20-year ZINCALUME roofing warranty cover in moderate environments and 25 years in mild environments. Those are warranty periods, not roof-expiry dates. The same page excludes more severe exposures from its recommendations, so site classification belongs in product selection.

COLORSTEEL’s newer MAXAM material replaced Endura and Maxx in its range. A warranty statement about an older product cannot simply be pasted onto a new specification, or vice versa. Match the exact product and applicable warranty document.

items: Which product and manufacturing period does the warranty apply to?
Does it cover perforation, paint performance, workmanship or something else?
What maintenance records are required?
Which flashings, fasteners and rainwater components are included?
Does the warranty transfer to a new owner? Ask for the written terms.

sections.title: What information helps decide between maintenance and reroofing?

blocks.text: Ask for a condition report that distinguishes isolated repairable details from widespread deterioration. It should identify the affected roof planes and components, describe the findings, and explain why the recommended scope addresses them. A useful report is more specific than an age estimate or a sales claim.

Record the roof’s approximate age if known, past repairs, current leaks, coating, coastal or industrial exposure, and any inaccessible or unwashed areas. Manufacturer maintenance requirements are relevant to both performance and warranty compliance.
A photo or this guide cannot diagnose concealed corrosion, structural condition or asbestos. Do not climb onto a roof to investigate. Use existing documents and obtain a competent assessment.

sections.title: Does maintenance mean replacing the roof?

blocks.text: Not necessarily. Treat inspection, maintenance, local repair and whole-roof replacement as separate options to be evaluated. Ask for the remaining uncertainties and the expected purpose of each recommendation, rather than assuming that a coating refresh automatically renews the whole roofing system.

NZMRM guidance explains that maintenance must reflect the material, environment and manufacturer instructions. Areas not naturally rain-washed can need different attention. Do not substitute a generic cleaning frequency for the instructions for the installed product.

sections.title: Why age alone is an incomplete answer

blocks.text: The lesson is not that every old roof has the same concealed damage. It is that a visual age estimate cannot establish the state of everything beneath the covering. Budget decisions should account for the evidence available and the work needed to confirm it.

sections.title: What should you request from a roofer?

items: A roof-specific condition report, ideally with annotated photographs taken safely.
Separate options for urgent work, planned repairs and replacement where appropriate.
Clear identification of the product and site exposure.
A scope for flashings, fixings and substrate, not just the visible sheets.
A written explanation of warranties and exclusions.

tile-to-metal.title: Can you replace a concrete tile roof with metal roofing?
tile-to-metal.description: NZ concrete-tile-to-metal reroof guidance: scope, consent checks, uplift, battens, hidden repairs and comparing complete replacement quotes.
tile-to-metal.answer: Yes, a tile-to-metal replacement can be feasible, but it is not simply a matter of ordering lighter sheets. The roof’s support, fixings, uplift resistance, geometry and proposed details need assessment. Whether the work is exempt from building consent depends on the actual work, not just the fact that the new covering is metal.

sections.title: Does changing the material always need building consent?

blocks.text: MBIE’s exemption guidance includes an example of replacing old clay tiles with profiled metal in the same position, while noting the need to consider increased wind uplift. It is an example under defined conditions, not automatic approval for every concrete-tile conversion. Confirm your scope with the designer and council where necessary.

Do not rely on either blanket statement: “all reroofs need consent” or “lighter roofing never needs consent”. Structural changes, the condition of the existing system and the details of the replacement can change the answer.

sections.title: What changes in the quote?

blocks.caption: Tile-to-metal scope comparison
heads: What to establish before comparing prices

cells: Existing material, access, disposal destination and whether the quoted rate covers the whole operation.
Whether existing support can be retained, or purlins/battens, connections or strengthening need work.
The proposed build-up and junction details, including penetrations.
How the new covering meets eaves, barges, gutters and existing features.
An opening-up allowance and agreed variation process for discoveries.
Access system, property protection, weather plan and hire duration.

blocks.text: A lower cladding weight does not remove the need for the roof assembly to resist wind. Ask the contractor or designer to explain the complete system rather than accepting “it is lighter” as a structural assessment.

sections.title: Which metal system should you compare?

blocks.text: Request options that are compatible with the measured pitch and roof layout. The appearance of long-run corrugate, a trapezoidal sheet and a pressed metal tile is different, but so are their component schedules. A tray option may require a different support build-up again.

Gerard Bond, for example, is a panel-based product with a stated 12° minimum. Metalcraft MC760 is a long-run profile with a published 3° starting minimum. Those figures are not enough to select a product without the manufacturer’s complete design requirements.

sections.title: How should you estimate the conversion cost?

blocks.text: Use: new roofing system + old-covering removal/disposal + access + separately defined repairs and extras. When comparing an all-in reroof quote, first identify which of these it already contains. Do not layer the same allowances on again.

RoofHub’s detailed estimator uses a separate removal line. Its working rates are planning inputs, not a supplier promise or a hazardous-materials quote. For a tile-to-metal conversion, unresolved support work can be more important than a small difference in sheet price.

sections.title: What can published reroofs teach us?

blocks.text: These are examples of associated upgrades and concealed work, not documented concrete-tile-to-metal price samples. We do not relabel them to make the evidence appear more complete.

sections.title: What if you are not sure which tile you have?

blocks.text: Concrete tiles, older textured metal tiles and asbestos-cement products should not be treated as the same material. A visual guess should not select a non-asbestos removal rate. Obtain appropriate identification before work that might disturb suspect material.

items: Keep any old installation or product paperwork.
Describe what is known and what is uncertain to the contractor.
Do not break, drill, scrape or pressure-wash suspect roofing to identify it.
Request a scope-specific assessment before agreeing to a removal price.

colorsteel-zincalume.title: COLORSTEEL vs ZINCALUME: what are you comparing?
colorsteel-zincalume.description: Compare current NZ COLORSTEEL and ZINCALUME terminology, coatings, site exposure and roof specifications, including changes to products since 2025.
colorsteel-zincalume.answer: COLORSTEEL is a prepainted steel roofing and cladding range; ZINCALUME is a metallic-coated steel product. Neither name identifies a roof profile. Compare the current product, exposure suitability and warranty as well as the colour and installed price. Older AZ-coating and Endura/Maxx descriptions need dating.

sections.title: What do the names tell you?

blocks.caption: Separate material, finish and shape

cells: Current product grade, profile, thickness, colour and site suitability.
Product generation, profile, thickness and exposure suitability.
Base material, coating, support and fixing details.

blocks.text: A meaningful comparison is not “COLORSTEEL versus corrugate”. One is a material brand and the other is a shape. Ask suppliers to quote the same shape and complete installation scope in the candidate materials.

sections.title: Why older articles can now be misleading

blocks.text: COLORSTEEL states that MAXAM replaced Endura and Maxx. Historical pricing tables using the old names remain evidence of what was published at the time, not current product recommendations.

New Zealand Steel’s current ZINCALUME page describes the move in 2025 from the previous AZ coating to an aluminium/zinc/magnesium AM125 coating using ACTIVATE technology. A comparison that describes every current ZINCALUME sheet using the old alloy alone is out of date.

Existing roofs and new orders are different questions. Identify the installed product from records where possible. Do not assume an older roof has the current coating or that a new product inherits an old warranty unchanged.

sections.title: Which one suits a coastal property?

blocks.text: Use the manufacturer’s exposure assessment, not a single generic distance-from-sea rule. New Zealand Steel does not recommend ZINCALUME for severe and more aggressive exposure categories on its current product page. Ask the supplier to confirm suitability in writing for the actual location.

Get the same assessment for the proposed prepainted product. A colour selection is not confirmation of corrosion suitability. The complete specification should also address compatible flashings, fasteners and any special details.

items: Provide the actual site and known exposure conditions.
Ask for the exact current product name on the quote.
Get the applicable warranty and maintenance requirements.
Confirm the specification covers the whole assembly, not just the visible roof sheets.

sections.title: Can RoofHub publish a reliable price premium?

blocks.text: Not yet as one national percentage. A matched pair would need the same supplier, profile, thickness, length, order date, freight and GST treatment. A material-only quote also cannot be compared directly with an installed package.

Our source register keeps historical mixed-scope cost guides separate from current specifications. It does not treat a supplier’s broad price range across several coatings as the cost difference between two named coatings.

sections.title: Which lasts longer?

blocks.text: A general durability ranking needs comparable exposure, maintenance and failure definitions. We do not use a maximum advertised warranty as an average roof life. Read the actual terms, including what is covered and which conditions apply.

For an existing roof, a condition assessment is more useful than a brand-only lifespan estimate. For a new roof, the first question is whether the product is appropriate for the site, followed by the detailing and maintenance needed to keep it performing.

sections.title: A better way to ask for two quotes

items: Use one drawing and measurement basis for both options.
Keep the roof profile, thickness and accessory scope the same where technically appropriate.
Show material, installation, removal and access scope clearly.
Ask each supplier to identify any specification change needed for site suitability.
Compare the final GST-inclusive totals only after aligning the scope.

timeline.title: How long does a reroof take in New Zealand?
timeline.description: Compare published NZ reroof durations, distinguish installation time from booking and scaffold hire, and plan for weather, hidden work and occupied homes.
timeline.answer: Published NZ contractor examples range from a two-day long-run job to work taking roughly a week, while general provider guidance extends further for complex projects. Do not confuse days on the roof with the time from enquiry to completion. Design, procurement, access and weather belong in the programme too.

sections.title: What do different businesses actually publish?

blocks.caption: Reported projects and general guidance are different evidence

cells: Hibiscus Coast project report. Area and price not published.
General FAQ, not a sample average.
3–5 working days for straightforward projects; longer for complex work
Provider planning guidance, not a guaranteed deadline.
Provider-specific offer with conditions, not a market standard.

blocks.text: These observations are not five equivalent experiments. Project size, crew, weather and scope are not standardised, so taking their mean would create false precision. They are useful prompts for discussing a programme with your chosen roofer.

sections.title: Which clock is being quoted?

blocks.caption: Break the project into stages

cells: Survey, scope, product availability, design or consent checks where relevant.
Access, storage, deliveries and protection of occupied areas.
How the old covering is removed and how temporary weather protection is managed.
Repairs, insulation, rainwater work and other trades.
Checks, cleaning, documentation and scaffold dismantling.

blocks.text: Request the roofing start date, expected on-site duration and likely scaffold removal date separately. A roof can be finished while access remains for painting or windows, and an early scaffold installation does not mean the roof work has started.

sections.title: What should the weather plan cover?

blocks.text: Ask who decides whether work proceeds, how forecasts are considered, how partially completed work is protected, and how a delay changes the programme. Those practical details are more useful than a promise to finish within a fixed number of days regardless of conditions.

Do not assume an occupied home must be completely uncovered at once. Ask the contractor to explain the sequence and protection plan for your building, rather than applying a generic installation sequence from an article.

sections.title: Why do some replacements take longer?

blocks.text: The examples show two different causes: previously hidden work and several trades sharing access. Neither should be treated as ordinary roofing labour silently included in every per-m² figure.

sections.title: How does timing affect scaffold cost?

blocks.text: Read the hire period in the scaffold quote. RoofHub’s detailed estimator models four included weeks and additional weekly hire, but that is a planning convention, not a standard offer from every scaffolder. Confirm when hire starts, minimum periods and who authorises extensions.
The number of roofing days cannot by itself determine rental cost. If access is erected before roofing, or retained for other work, its hire clock can be longer.

items: Is there a separate setup and dismantling price?
How much hire is included?
What is the extra weekly rate and GST basis?
Who pays when another trade needs the scaffold longer?
What notice is required for dismantling?

sections.title: What should an occupied household know?

items: Daily access arrangements and safe exclusion areas.
Whether pets, vehicles, outdoor furniture or garden areas need moving.
Who communicates delays or unexpected work.
How any services, penetrations or insulation work affect occupants.
The emergency contact and temporary-weather-protection plan.

decramastic.title: Does Decramastic roofing contain asbestos?
decramastic.description: What NZ homeowners should do before repairing, cleaning or removing older textured roofing, with current WorkSafe sources and clear estimate exclusions.
decramastic.answer: Some older textured metal roofing can contain asbestos. The name, appearance or a photograph cannot reliably establish that a particular roof is asbestos-free. Before work that could disturb suspect material, arrange appropriate identification and assessment. Do not pressure-wash, scrape or break it to investigate.

sections.title: Why does this need checking before quoting?

blocks.text: WorkSafe’s August 2026 safety alert describes asbestos contamination after high-pressure washing of an older Decramastic roof. Its message is to check before this work, not to assume every textured roof has the same composition.

A routine roof-removal allowance is not an asbestos-removal quote. Identification can change the required work method, people involved, containment, cleanup and disposal arrangements. Those decisions need to be made before the roof is disturbed.

sections.title: How should uncertainty be handled?

items: Tell the contractor that the material is unknown or suspected.
Look for product and installation records without disturbing the roof.
Ask a competent asbestos professional how identification or testing should be arranged.
Do not take a DIY sample based on instructions from a general roofing article.
Keep the result and the agreed removal scope with your project documents.

blocks.text: This page is not an identification service. Selecting “Decramastic” or “unknown” in an estimator must not silently produce a confirmed non-asbestos removal price.

sections.title: What should a roofing estimate include or exclude?

blocks.caption: Keep ordinary removal separate from unresolved hazardous work

cells: Material confirmed suitable for ordinary removal
Show assessment as unresolved; label any ordinary roofing total as excluding that unresolved work.
Obtain a specialist scope-specific assessment and quote.
Roof already disturbed or contamination suspected
Stop the affected work and obtain professional advice; do not use a normal cleaning allowance.

blocks.text: A useful budget can still show the proposed new roof separately. It must make clear that the replacement-covering number is not the cost of safely removing the old material. An unpriced item is not a zero-cost item.

sections.title: Is cleaning a harmless way to check the roof?

blocks.text: No. WorkSafe warns against high-pressure water and compressed air on asbestos-containing materials. Do not treat cleaning as an identification test or a way to postpone assessment.

Where the product is uncertain, provide the contractor with that uncertainty rather than choosing the cheapest cleaning or removal option. Photographs taken from a safe place can help describe the roof, but cannot certify its composition.

sections.title: What should you ask the contractor?

items: Who will identify the material, and how will the result be documented?
Does the quote assume a negative result, or include specialist work?
What changes if the result is positive?
Who is responsible for the safe work and disposal arrangements?
What evidence of completion and any required clearance will be supplied?

faqs.q: Can you tell from a roof photo whether it contains asbestos?
faqs.a: No. A photograph is not a reliable asbestos identification result. Arrange appropriate assessment before disturbing suspect material.

roofing-costs.title: How much does roofing cost in New Zealand?
roofing-costs.description: Compare NZ roof prices by scope, with dated supplier and contractor observations, visible GST, roof-area examples and practical quoting tools.
roofing-costs.answer: For broad planning, Edwards & Hardy’s March 2026 NZ guide lists long-run roof replacement at $15,000–$35,000 per job and metal tile at $17,000–$45,000. These are publisher estimates, not prices for one fixed roof size, and GST treatment is not stated. A new-build roof or a sheet-only price has a different scope: compare area, products, removal and access before comparing totals.

sections.title: What prices have NZ businesses actually published?

blocks.text: These observations are not directly interchangeable. The Edwards & Hardy figures are whole-job estimates without a single fixed roof size or stated GST treatment. Delta’s figures are from a 2025 guide and include a wider reroof scope. We retain the date rather than relabel them as this year’s price list.
A source can be correctly recorded and still be too broad or old for your quote. “Checked” means the quoted information was found, not that RoofHub independently verified the cost of a completed job.

sections.title: What does “roofing cost per m²” include?

blocks.caption: Choose the right pricing basis

cells: The purchased sheet, tile or component.
Cover width, gauge, finish, tax, freight and accessories.
Work covered by the installer’s rate.
Which preparation, underlay and flashing tasks are included.
A stated combination of products and labour.
Whether battens, substrate, underlay, fixings and flashings are in the scope.
Replacement work with specified removal and project costs.
Access, hazardous materials, hidden repairs and rainwater work.

blocks.text: A cheap material rate and a complete-project quote answer different questions. Compare them only after identifying the missing work. The arithmetic can be perfectly correct while the scope comparison is wrong.

sections.title: Which metal roof is cheapest?

blocks.text: There is not enough like-for-like evidence here to declare one system universally cheapest. Pressed metal tile, corrugate and five-rib should be compared on the same building with the same inclusions. An estimated price comparison is not a measured national ranking.

Architectural tray is also a family, not one build-up. A system fixed over purlins and a curved aluminium roof over plywood do not have the same components. Ask for the named system and its support requirements.
Historical low-end pressed-tile figures in older guides are not current wholesale material prices. They should not be used to force a new installed-price hierarchy.

sections.title: How do you turn a rate into a useful budget?

blocks.text: For an actual 200m² sloping roof and a hypothetical all-in rate of $150–$200/m² including GST, the arithmetic is $30,000–$40,000 including GST. If the rate already includes scaffold and removal, adding them again overstates the budget. If it excludes them, leaving them out understates it.
A whole-house figure can be useful for planning, but the detailed estimator separates measured components. Ridge, hip, valley and barge lengths are not determined by area alone.

sections.title: What can completed projects explain?

blocks.text: These six published examples cover different constraints. None supplies a comparable final bill and roof area together, so they support scope explanations rather than a price-per-m² dataset. Follow the original project links for the publishers’ photography and full accounts.

sections.title: How do you compare two quotes fairly?

items: Use the same actual roof area and a consistent wastage policy.
Match product, coating, thickness and accessory specification.
Identify what is included for underlay, battens or substrate.
Keep removal, disposal and access visible.
Record exclusions and the process for unforeseen work.
Compare the complete totals on the same GST basis.

blocks.text: Before accepting a low figure, ask what would cause it to change. An estimate becomes more useful when its exclusions are explicit, not when they are hidden in a smaller headline number.

sections.title: What is still missing from this evidence?

blocks.text: Public sources rarely provide all of area, pitch, final paid price, GST, specification and inclusions. The current collection is not a representative survey and does not support precise city premiums, national medians or advertised percentage savings. RoofHub will add those comparisons only when the underlying sample supports them.

faqs.q: Does RoofHub quote the cheapest roof in NZ?
faqs.a: No. The current evidence does not establish a universally cheapest system. Compare the same building, product specification, tax basis and installed scope.

faqs.q: Are source prices guaranteed offers?
faqs.a: No. Some are dated published guides and some are retail listings. Check the source date, unit, GST and current availability before relying on any figure.

reroof-cost.title: What does a reroof cost in New Zealand?
reroof-cost.description: Understand reroof pricing as replacement plus removal, access and defined extras, with NZ project examples, asbestos cautions and a like-for-like quote checklist.
reroof-cost.answer: Published reroof guides give useful starting points, not fixed offers. Delta’s 2025 guide puts corrugated replacements for a 150–200m² home at $18,000–$28,000 including GST, scaffold, old-roof removal, materials and labour. Keep that date and scope attached to the figure. Your budget still needs the existing material, actual roof area and any separately identified repairs or upgrades.

sections.title: What does the published pricing cover?

blocks.text: These are contractor guide figures, not anonymised invoices. Compare their dates and GST treatment as carefully as their endpoints. A complete-reroof rate should not be used as a sheet-and-labour rate and then have removal and scaffold added a second time.

sections.title: How does the old roof change the job?

blocks.caption: Existing roof and estimating implications

cells: Removal and handling scope, existing support condition and new profile compatibility.
Panel and batten work, underlay condition and the chosen replacement system.
Handling/disposal and the design implications of the proposed new covering.
Material identification before assuming ordinary removal.

blocks.text: Do not use roof area plus a single “reroof premium” where the included work remains unknown. A separate removal line makes the assumptions visible and makes it possible to replace an allowance with a real contractor quote.

sections.title: What is the cleanest estimating structure?

blocks.text: Use one set of roof quantities for the new system. Add the removal/disposal scope against the actual area being stripped, without adding a new-sheet waste allowance to that area. Add measured or separately estimated access. List repairs, hazardous work and optional upgrades distinctly.

items: New covering and compatible flashings.
Underlay, fixings and support work appropriate to that system.
Removal, disposal and transport.
Scaffold or other assessed safe access.
Insulation, gutters, downpipes and repairs only where selected or required.
A clear unresolved-items allowance or exclusion, not a zero.

sections.title: Why do similar-looking reroofs have different scopes?

blocks.text: The useful comparison is what the work included. These accounts do not supply enough comparable cost data to establish a normal price, but they show why timing and associated repairs cannot be inferred from roofing material alone.

sections.title: What if the roof could contain asbestos?

blocks.text: WorkSafe identifies roofing among products that can contain asbestos. Uncertain older material should be assessed before disturbance, not assumed negative because a price calculator needs a number.
For suspect material, the ordinary replacement estimate excludes unresolved asbestos assessment/removal. Obtain the appropriate professional advice before agreeing a complete project scope.

sections.title: Does a reroof need consent?

blocks.text: MBIE provides examples of replacement work that can fall within an exemption and explains limitations. The answer depends on your work, including any structural changes and the condition being remedied. Do not rely on a contractor blog’s blanket yes or no.

Who provides access and how long hire is included.
What happens if damage is uncovered.
What is excluded from the price and who approves variations.
The installation programme, weather plan and completion documents.

long-run.title: What is long-run roofing, and which profile do you need?
long-run.description: NZ long-run roofing explained through corrugate, trapezoidal and architectural profiles, current product specifications, price units and project examples.
long-run.answer: Long-run roofing uses sheets formed to the required lengths rather than small individual tiles. Corrugate and five-rib are familiar profile families, but a complete specification must also identify the base material, coating, thickness, fixing and support system. Start with the roof’s design constraints, then compare price on a matched scope.

sections.title: Which profile families should you compare?

blocks.caption: Long-run profile families and examples

cells: Rounded appearance and exact product pitch requirements.
Rib geometry, cover, support and drainage requirements.
Concealed fixing, support build-up and seam detailing.

blocks.text: The word “long-run” does not mean every product can be laid at the same pitch. Nor does “standing seam” identify one universal construction method. Ask for the exact product details before making a material takeoff.

sections.title: What needs to be on the specification?

items: Manufacturer and full profile name.
Effective cover, sheet lengths and base metal thickness where specified.
Base metal, coating product and colour.
Roof pitch, local exposure and design loads assessed by the responsible professional.
Compatible supports, underlay, fasteners, flashings and penetrations.
Warranty, maintenance instructions and any transport/access restrictions.

blocks.text: A project can fail a budget comparison before anyone does arithmetic: two “metal roof” prices might include different coatings, thicknesses and edge details. A shared specification makes comparison useful.

sections.title: Why do lineal and square-metre prices differ?

blocks.text: A lineal metre is one metre along a sheet. Its usable area is that length multiplied by the effective cover width. Divide the per-lineal-metre price by effective cover in metres to get sheet-only cost per square metre. Installation, cutting, laps at sheet ends and accessories remain separate.

sections.title: What minimum pitch applies?

blocks.text: Published starting minima include 8° for Metalcraft Corrugate and 3° for MC760. These are tied to those products; sheet length and other design conditions can raise the requirement. A general “metal roofing minimum” is not a safe specification.
Your plan’s roof pitch also changes surface area. A horizontal measurement needs conversion; an actual sloping measurement does not. Use separate inputs for roof planes with different pitches.

sections.title: How is long-run used on actual roofs?

blocks.text: The examples range from a villa replacement to angular sheets and a curved architectural roof. This is why one long-run price band cannot describe every system and detail.

sections.title: What pricing evidence is useful?

blocks.text: That retail sheet listing does not describe a complete local roll-formed COLORSTEEL installation. For a project budget, use a written matched specification or the separate scope-based observations in the roofing-cost guide.

sections.title: What should you decide before asking for a price?

blocks.text: First settle the suitable profile and material with the supplier or designer. Then establish area, component lengths and site access. Comparing complete quotes becomes much easier when the same roof geometry and scope are used by everyone.

corrugated.title: Corrugated roofing NZ: prices, profiles and real projects
corrugated.description: Compare NZ corrugated roofing prices, effective cover, 0.40 and 0.55 mm steel, pitch and coatings. Check supplier evidence, seven projects and your own roof budget.
corrugated.answer: Corrugated roofing is long-run metal sheeting with a rounded wave profile. Price depends on the exact profile, metal thickness, coating and job scope. This guide compares named NZ supplier prices, six manufacturers and seven published projects, then helps you calculate a sheet budget or estimate a complete roof.

sections.title: How much does corrugated roofing cost?

blocks.text: There are three different questions: what a sheet costs, what a new roof costs to supply and fit, and what an existing roof costs to replace. Start with the scope, not the lowest number. The current listing review below is a set of named offers, not a survey establishing one typical New Zealand price.

cells: See the current listing ledger below. Prices are preserved in the supplier’s original unit.
No installation, flashings, underlay, fixings, freight or removal is implied.

Historical long-run guidance, not a current corrugate-only rate. Do not multiply by pitched area as if it were the same basis.

blocks.text: Choose a source-specific example or enter a quote you already have. The calculation uses actual roof area, effective cover and any allowance you explicitly choose. A sheet subtotal is deliberately kept separate from a complete roof estimate.

blocks.title: Compare 100, 150, 200 and 250 m² examples

blocks.text: These examples hold area constant to expose the scope difference. They are not four completed jobs. Real sheet orders need roof-plane widths, cut lengths and waste; a contractor quote also needs the other components. A 200 m² floor area is not automatically a 200 m² roof.

sections.title: Are all corrugated profiles the same?

blocks.text: No. “Corrugate” describes a shape family, not a single specification. “Long-run” describes the sheet format; COLORSTEEL and ZINCALUME describe branded steel products, not the wave shape. A quote should identify the rollformer, profile, thickness and coating, rather than simply saying “corrugated iron”.

blocks.caption: NZ manufacturer comparison: check the current drawing for the specified product

cells: Sheet width is 851 mm. Its guide increases the pitch requirement for longer sheets and states a rainfall assumption.
Sheet width is 851 mm. Check its material-specific span and fixing tables.
Approximate dimensions are not a guarantee that another maker’s sheet will lap correctly.
The Roofing Store specifies 0.40 and 0.55 mm BMT G550 options and different design conditions.
Confirm current drawing; Roof Crowd quotes 762 mm
Retailer cover information is identified as retailer information, not silently promoted to a checked manufacturer drawing.
Special deeper profile; see the Herne Bay account
Not ordinary shallow corrugate. Do not transfer its low-pitch claims to a generic sheet.

blocks.title: Why effective cover changes the price and quantity

blocks.text: One metre of a sheet with 760 mm usable cover covers 0.760 m², not one square metre. At 762 mm, it covers 0.762 m². Effective cover already allows for the designed side lap: do not deduct the side lap a second time. Cut lengths, end laps and offcuts still require a separate takeoff.

For a simple rectangular plane 10 m wide across the corrugations, 760 mm cover requires 14 full sheets across: round 10 ÷ 0.760 up, not down. That is a geometric example, not a cutting plan or an approved installation detail. A width-only calculation cannot price hips and valleys.

sections.title: Which thickness and roof pitch do I need?

blocks.text: Treat thickness, profile and pitch as design inputs, not an upgrade menu. NZMRM explains that load performance also depends on steel grade and profile shape. More thickness does not cancel an unsuitable roof pitch, an underspecified fixing pattern or an incompatible coating.

blocks.title: 0.40 versus 0.55 mm: what to ask for

blocks.caption: Thickness comparison, not a substitute for structural design

cells: A standard option in residential corrugate ranges.
Also offered for corrugate where the design calls for it.
More vulnerable to foot-traffic damage according to NZMRM.
Greater robustness can be useful where maintenance access or loads justify it.
Span, grade, wind load, fasteners, coating and safe access.
The same factors. A thicker sheet is not permission to walk on an unassessed roof.

blocks.text: BMT means base metal thickness, before metallic and paint coatings. A merchant description saying only “0.5 mm gauge” has not necessarily confirmed BMT. Request the product specification rather than treating 0.5 mm, 0.40 BMT and 0.55 BMT as directly interchangeable.

Price comparisons should match grade as well as thickness. NZMRM specifically warns against replacing specified 0.55 mm G550 with G300 for straight corrugate. We have not derived a “0.55 premium” by comparing different shops and coatings.

blocks.title: Minimum pitch: why 8° is common but not universal

blocks.text: Ordinary NZ corrugate product pages commonly state 8°. The current NZMRM generic table distinguishes shallow corrugate from deeper profiles and requires runoff checks. Its minimum refers to the installed cladding pitch, not just the angle drawn on a plan. Roof run, rainfall, deflection and junctions still matter.

For example, Metalcraft describes 8° after deflection for sheets up to 30 m and 9° for longer sheets below 50 m, under its stated rainfall assumption. Freeman separately calls for at least 10° where its corrugate is end-lapped. These conditions are precisely why the shortest headline specification is not enough.

The Herne Bay project attributes a 4° capability to the special True Oak product used there. That is evidence of a profile-specific solution, not permission to use any corrugated sheet at 4°. Have the current product, pitch and water-carrying capacity checked for the actual roof.

blocks.title: Not sure whether you have plan or actual measurements?
blocks.text: Work out the pitch and area basis before comparing quotes. Use plans or safely obtained measurements; do not climb onto the roof to supply an input.
blocks.label: Understand roof pitch

sections.title: COLORSTEEL, ZINCALUME and coastal roofs

blocks.text: Corrugated is the shape. The substrate, metallic coating and paint system are separate choices. New Zealand Steel describes a change to ZINCALUME’s coating technology in 2025, so old articles about its composition should not be treated as the current specification.

blocks.title: Choose a coating for the site, not just a colour

blocks.caption: Specification questions for your supplier

cells: Exact current product and warranty conditions, not just “Colorsteel colour”.
A colour description does not identify the substrate or coating system.
Exact metallic coating and the environments approved by its supplier.
ZINCALUME is a branded material specification; a listing saying “zinc” may not establish the same product.
Exposure category, sheltered areas, runoff and incompatible materials.
Distance from the sea alone is not enough to promise suitability or a warranty.
Distinguish the product used then from what is supplied now.
An old ENDURA or MAXX project is not a current warranty recommendation.

blocks.text: Request written confirmation of suitability for the address and the selected accessories. The coating decision should include flashings and fasteners, not just the roof sheets. Use the current supplier details for incompatible contacts and runoff.

blocks.text: Read the material comparison before comparing their totals.

sections.title: What should a corrugated roof quote include?

blocks.text: Ask for a roof system and a defined scope, not a sheet rate multiplied by floor area. The following is RoofHub’s comparison checklist. Whether an item is included, excluded, retained or a provisional allowance should be explicit.

items: Named profile, coating, colour, BMT and steel grade, with measured roof-plane areas and a stated waste or cutting allowance.
Ridges, hips, valleys, barges, aprons and penetration flashings, with lengths or a clearly defined inclusion.
Compatible fixings, underlay and any required support, plus agreed ventilation details.
For a reroof: existing material, removal, disposal and the process for suspected hazardous material.
Access, scaffold or edge protection: assessed scope, hire duration and any additional weekly cost.
Timber repairs, insulation, guttering, downpipes and skylights: included, excluded or provisional.
Delivery, lifting, site protection, clean-up, GST, payment stages and product/workmanship warranty terms.

blocks.title: Underlay, ventilation and flashings are not optional details

blocks.text: NZMRM describes absorbent underlay as a way to hold condensation temporarily until it can evaporate. It explicitly cautions against treating underlay as a reliable second roof or using it to compensate for poor weatherproofing. Support and product selection depend on the assembly.

For reroofing, the code recommends no more than one compliant layer, apart from laps. An old layer should not automatically be left in place with another laid over it. Excess moisture also needs its cause addressed, including moisture entering the cavity and ventilation, rather than simply adding more underlay.

A standard $/m² covering allowance cannot count the actual hips, valleys or roof-to-wall junctions. Measure those lineal items separately in a detailed takeoff. Do not assume that a labour rate for fixing sheets also includes fabrication of every flashing.

blocks.title: Already have areas and flashing lengths?
blocks.text: The detailed tool lets you enter those quantities rather than guess a house-size category. Confirm every included and unpriced component before treating its result as a project budget.
blocks.label: Use my measurements

sections.title: What do real NZ projects show?

blocks.text: These seven accounts come from six different publishers. They show decisions made on identifiable projects, not seven independently verified prices. None of the selected accounts supplies both a measured roof area and a final roof price, so we do not manufacture a cost per square metre. Photographs remain on the original publishers’ websites.

sections.title: Repair it, replace it, or change the material?

blocks.text: First establish whether the problem is an isolated detail, deterioration across the sheets, moisture from inside the roof, or work hidden underneath. A photo cannot establish all four. Obtain a roof assessment before comparing a local repair price with a replacement budget.

blocks.title: Replacement scope, consent and asbestos

blocks.text: MBIE’s guidance includes exempt replacement of old profiled metal roofing with a comparable assembly. It also gives a heavy-tile-to-metal example, while requiring uplift effects to be considered. Substantial structural work, premature durability failure and other exceptions can change the answer. Do not assume either that every reroof needs consent or that none does; confirm the actual scope with the council or designer.

Where older roofing or associated material may contain asbestos, arrange competent identification before disturbing it. Corrugated-looking material can be fibre cement rather than steel. Do not drill, cut, break or pressure-wash suspect material to work out what it is. Testing and specialist removal, where required, belong outside an ordinary metal-removal allowance.

Scaffolding and edge protection are site-safety arrangements, not just optional price add-ons. WorkSafe’s guidance covers fitness for purpose and safe design. Let a competent provider determine the arrangement for the actual pitch, height, ground conditions and work sequence.

blocks.title: Replacing an existing roof?
blocks.text: Compare the covering, removal and access scopes separately before combining them.
blocks.label: See reroof costs and inclusions

sections.title: How long will a corrugated roof last?

blocks.text: There is no single lifespan established by the wave shape. NZMRM distinguishes Building Code durability requirements from useful life. A warranty has its own conditions too. Product choice, the environment, detailing and maintenance all need to be considered before attaching a lifespan to a particular roof.

blocks.title: What to check after installation and over time

blocks.text: A 15-year durability reference is not an instruction to replace every roof at year 15, nor a promise that all components last equally long. Hidden, difficult-to-replace elements can have different durability obligations. Check the actual assembly and product documents.

COLORSTEEL care guidance emphasises areas that rain does not wash, accumulated debris and ongoing maintenance. Arrange safe gutter and roof care and keep maintenance records; do not assume a coating makes the whole roof maintenance-free. Ask your installer how to check flashings, penetrations and later additions such as solar equipment without damaging the sheets.
Treat online “40-year” or “50-year” claims as claims to investigate, not evidence that a coating warranty, a weather-tightness obligation and the building’s service life are all the same period.

blocks.title: Need the full distinction between service life and warranty?
blocks.text: Use the lifespan guide to understand the questions to ask before accepting a long-life claim.

cells: Angular ribs and often different pitch and drainage capabilities. Names and cover widths differ by maker.
Match coating, grade, BMT and effective cover. Include flashing and cutting labour, not just sheet prices.
Smaller overlapping panels with a different support and accessory system.
Compare a complete roof-system quote. A historical tile price and a current corrugate sheet price are not a valid cheapest-roof test.
A different seam, fixing and detailing system rather than simply a wider corrugation.
Check substrate/support and installation scope against the selected system.

blocks.text: Send the same project brief to each contractor: the same area basis, product, access assumptions, removal scope and repair allowances. RoofHub’s tools help you organise that brief; the written site-specific quotation is where those assumptions are confirmed.

sections.title: How was this guide checked?

blocks.text: We use manufacturer and NZMRM information for technical comparisons, supplier listings for material observations, and attributed contractor accounts for project context. A check establishes what a source states; it does not independently certify the product, inspect the project or verify a transaction.

blocks.title: Read the calculation and evidence rules

items: Each price retains its original unit, tax basis, source and check date. Unknown does not become zero or “included”.
Per-sheet prices are divided only by their stated length. Per-m² conversion also requires source-specific effective cover.
GST is added at 15% only to a price explicitly excluding GST. Unknown tax basis is not silently converted.
Archived seller dimensions and approximate cover are labelled. Conditional conversions do not become certified specifications.
Historical installed guides are not inflation-adjusted or blended with material-only listings. No national average or median is inferred.
Supplier variants count as listings, not independent suppliers. Sources owned by related organisations are not assumed independent corroboration.
Seconds, recycled stock and Musgroves restocking prices are excluded from this new-roof review. Ambiguous current listings remain visible as unresolved checks, not cheap offers.
None of this changes the estimator’s numeric rate card. No imagery, measured roof area, price or outcome is invented for the project accounts.

blocks.text: For a quoted price R per lineal metre and confirmed cover W millimetres, sheet coverage rate = R ÷ (W ÷ 1,000). For one roof pitch θ, sloping area = horizontal projected roof area ÷ cos θ. The projection must include roof overhangs. These are geometric conversions, not allowances for cuts, end laps or complex roof intersections.

A review date is not a supplier’s guarantee that a price is still available. Confirm the selected specification, quantity, delivery and validity when requesting a written quote. Sources below give you a direct route to check or challenge our interpretation.

faqs.q: Is corrugated roofing the same as COLORSTEEL?
faqs.a: No. Corrugated identifies the shape; COLORSTEEL identifies a branded prepainted steel product. A corrugated sheet can use different substrates and coatings. Ask for both the profile and the exact material.

faqs.q: How much does a 200 m² corrugated roof cost?
faqs.a: Sheet supply, new-roof installation and a complete reroof are different budgets. Use the size examples above, keeping their source date and inclusions attached. The measured sloping roof area, not automatically the home’s floor area, is the relevant quantity for a surface-area rate.

faqs.q: Can I use corrugated roofing at 5°?
faqs.a: Do not assume an ordinary 8° product is suitable. A deeper, specifically designed corrugated profile may have a different limit. Obtain the selected product’s current pitch and runoff requirements for the actual roof.

faqs.q: Is 0.55 mm always better than 0.40 mm?
faqs.a: It is not a substitute for a correct design. Compare base metal thickness and grade, loading, purlin spacing, fixings and coating. NZMRM identifies circumstances where greater thickness is useful, including greater expected roof traffic.

faqs.q: Can I order by dividing roof area by sheet width?
faqs.a: Not reliably. Use effective cover to estimate total lineal length, then measure each roof plane to establish full sheet counts and cut lengths. Areas alone cannot determine hips, valleys, offcuts or a manufacturable order.

faqs.q: Are the project examples RoofHub jobs?
faqs.a: No. They are attributed publisher accounts linked to the original businesses. We have not independently inspected them or verified an invoice. Missing prices and measured areas remain unpublished.

faqs.q: Can I get an estimate without giving my contact details?
faqs.a: Yes. The on-page arithmetic and detailed estimator are available before an enquiry. Entering your details is a separate step when you want to ask about your project.

five-rib.title: Five-rib roofing NZ: prices, profiles and real projects
five-rib.description: Compare eight NZ five-rib profile entries, five supplier listings and seven projects. Check cover, pitch and flashing differences, then calculate a sheet budget.
five-rib.answer: Five-rib roofing is a family of angular, ribbed metal profiles, not one standard sheet. NZ examples include MC760, T-Rib, Plumbdek, Hi Five, Veedek, Trimrib and TRS5. Start with the exact profile and its roof-specific requirements, then compare effective cover, coating, thickness and installed scope. The supplier prices below are for sheets only, not a complete roof.

sections.title: What does five-rib roofing cost?

blocks.text: The useful starting point is a named product, not one national five-rib rate. This review records five sheet listings from four businesses. Prices have different finishes, thickness descriptions and units. Only one currently supports a GST-inclusive area conversion, and even that cover measurement needs confirming against the seller’s current stock.

blocks.title: Looking for the whole roof, not just the sheets?
blocks.text: Add labour, matched flashings, underlay, removal and access in the detailed estimator. Its planning rate card is separate from these source-specific retail observations.

blocks.title: Why these listings are not a national supply-and-install range

blocks.text: We have not pooled the lowest and highest prices into a “typical” range. A painted sheet and an unpainted sheet are not the same specification. Nor are five listings from four businesses five independent confirmations of one price.

Bitz & Piecez appears in both our corrugate and five-rib reviews because its listing offers both profiles. It is still one business and one shared price observation, not two independently collected market samples.

The new-sheet listing at Renovation Warehouse is included because it explicitly describes new stock. Clearance, used, damaged or seconds stock is not a normal first-quality benchmark. Listing review dates do not guarantee today’s checkout price or availability.

sections.title: What would the sheets cost for my roof?

blocks.text: Use a quoted price with confirmed effective cover, or inspect the conditional supplier example below. Enter actual sloping area when you have it. A horizontal roof projection needs a pitch adjustment; a total floor-area figure across two storeys is not a roof measurement.

blocks.title: Read the calculation before using the result

blocks.text: Sheet-only allowance = actual roof area ÷ effective cover in metres × price per lineal metre. For one uniform pitch, actual roof area = horizontal roof projection ÷ cos(pitch). Enter the roof outline including eaves, not an unadjusted internal floor area.

The extra-material input is your allowance. Side laps are already reflected in effective cover. End laps, angled cuts and stock-length offcuts still need a plane-by-plane takeoff. A continuous-length allowance is not a count of whole sheets or a purchase order.

sections.title: Which NZ profiles belong in this comparison?

blocks.text: Compare named profile entries rather than treating every five-rib sheet as interchangeable. The table contains eight entries from six manufacturers; some entries are families with branch-dependent variants. A swage is an additional pan stiffener, not necessarily another major rib.

Hi Five needs a width check: Dimond’s page gives 765 mm in its overview and 755 mm in its performance table. We preserve the conflict rather than choosing the smaller price per square metre. Confirm the ordering dimension with the supplying branch.

blocks.title: Five-rib, six-rib, T-Rib, Trimrib and tray are not interchangeable names

blocks.text: Freeman lists Five Rib and Six Rib as different profiles. Rib count alone does not identify matching sheet geometry, accessories or an allowable span. If replacing one damaged sheet, provide the actual profile drawing or matching dimensions, not just “five-rib”.

Trimrib S, TS and V describe different pan-stiffener arrangements in the same family. MC760 and T-Rib are Metalcraft product names. Similar names on a quote do not establish identical manufacturing dimensions.
Architectural tray and standing-seam systems belong in a separate specification and pricing comparison. Do not confuse a five-rib roof profile with the coating brand or with a concealed-fix system.

blocks.text: Compare tray and standing seam separately from conventional ribbed long-run sheets.

sections.title: Why effective cover matters more than advertised width

blocks.caption: Example dimensions from named products, not interchangeable ordering sizes

blocks.text: An illustrative $25/lm quote at 760 mm cover gives $32.89 per covered square metre on the same GST basis. Using 810 mm overall width instead would give $30.86, understating that sheet-area cost by about 6.2%. This is arithmetic, not a published offer.

Two sheets with the same lineal rate can have different covered-area rates. That does not establish equivalent strength, coating, warranty or installed labour. Confirm both specifications before comparing their totals.

blocks.text: Use the side-by-side worksheet to put confirmed cover and GST on the same basis.

sections.title: Can five-rib go on a 3° roof?

blocks.text: Several named products publish a 3° starting minimum, but the number is conditional. Metalcraft specifically warns that its minimum increases with sheet length. A general “low-pitch” description cannot replace the current product manual and project design.

Freeman distinguishes a 3° starting minimum from a 10° condition for its end-lapped Five Rib roofing. That is a product-specific warning against assuming that a low-pitch rating also permits every lap arrangement.

Roof drainage must account for the actual finished slope. Ponding is not solved simply by selecting a different paint or corrosion-resistant coating. Confirm drainage and support design before ordering.

blocks.title: Useful information to give the supplier or designer

items: Pitch of each plane, including the lowest-pitch section.
Sheet run length and whether end laps or changes of pitch are proposed.
Purlin spacing, design loads and wind exposure, assessed by the appropriate professional.
Upstream catchments, gutters, penetrations and roof junctions.
Exact profile, metal, BMT and coating proposed.

blocks.text: This guide is a comparison aid, not an installation specification or structural approval. Follow the current manufacturer’s design information and the project’s applicable compliance requirements.

blocks.text: Convert rise and run, or see how pitch affects a plan-area measurement.

sections.title: 0.40, 0.55 or 0.5 mm: what are you actually comparing?

blocks.text: BMT means base metal thickness, before coatings. A retailer’s “0.5 mm gauge” is not automatically a 0.55 mm BMT product. Ask whether the dimension is base metal, total coated thickness or an unspecified listing description.

Plumbdek and TRS5 publish 0.40 and 0.55 mm BMT options. Their availability does not mean the thinner or thicker choice is correct for every support spacing and load. Use the selected product’s design tables and the project specification.

blocks.caption: Keep these specification decisions separate

cells: BMT where specified, rather than an unexplained gauge
Exposure, compatibility, warranty conditions and maintenance

blocks.title: A colour or brand name is not a complete specification

blocks.text: COLORSTEEL MAXAM and ColorCote MagnaFlow describe coating/material systems rather than a five-rib shape. Ask for the profile and coating separately. A project using a black low-gloss finish is an appearance example, not proof that every black roof has that specification.
Coastal suitability needs a site-specific material decision. Warranty conditions and maintenance requirements are not the same thing as a guaranteed roof lifespan.

sections.title: Does five-rib always need more expensive flashing work?

blocks.text: Not automatically. NZMRM’s flashing guidance allows soft-edge options on low trapezoidal profiles and prefers notched treatment for taller ribs over 30 mm. Roofing Industries’ Trimrib drawing directory includes soft-edge and scribed/notched ridge details. The actual specified detail matters more than a blanket rule that every five-rib roof must be hand-notched.

Where a chosen detail needs notching, angled cutting or complex intersections, ask the roofer to identify that work in the quote. The research here does not establish a universal labour percentage. RoofHub’s existing contributor-supplied estimator allowances remain model inputs, not a newly verified market tariff.

faqs.q: Is five-rib more expensive than corrugate?
faqs.a: Not inevitably. Bitz & Piecez lists both profiles at one lineal rate. Compare confirmed effective cover and equivalent specification first, then compare the labour and accessory scope. That listing is not a national installed-price study.

faqs.q: Is five-rib the same as fibreglass roofing?
faqs.a: No. This guide covers metal five-rib profiles. A similar rib pattern does not make a translucent sheet and a steel sheet the same product or structural specification.

faqs.q: Is Trimrib the same as T-Rib?
faqs.a: No. They are names used by different manufacturers. Confirm the exact profile, cover and matching details rather than ordering on a similar-sounding name.

faqs.q: How wide is five-rib roofing?
faqs.a: There is no single usable width for the family. Examples here include 755 mm Veedek, 760 mm MC760 and 765 mm Plumbdek. Use confirmed effective cover, not total sheet width.

faqs.q: Do six-rib sheets use the same measurements?
faqs.a: Do not assume so. Freeman publishes Five Rib and Six Rib separately. Match the actual profile drawing and accessories.

faqs.q: Does a 3° product rating approve my low-pitch roof?
faqs.a: No. Length, laps, drainage, support and installation conditions still apply. Confirm the selected product against the actual roof design.

faqs.q: Can the page give me a complete installed price?
faqs.a: The worksheet is sheet-only arithmetic. The detailed estimator adds project components using its separate planning assumptions. A supplier or roofer still needs to confirm measurements, specifications and scope for a proper quote.

pressed-tile.title: Pressed metal tile roofing NZ: prices, profiles and new-home examples
pressed-tile.description: Compare modern pressed-metal tile profiles, published NZ installed prices and complete-system costs. Calculate panel quantities, inspect new-home examples and plan a replacement.
pressed-tile.answer: Pressed metal tile is a lightweight steel-panel roof system for new homes as well as replacements, with smooth, stone-coated and concealed-fix choices. Price the whole system, not just the panels: underlay, battens or decking, matching trims, fixings and installation all matter. The published prices below have different dates and inclusions, so they are shown separately rather than presented as one current NZ price range.

sections.title: How much does pressed metal tile roofing cost?

blocks.text: Start with three different questions: what are the panels worth, what is the complete new-roof package, and what does replacing an old roof add? A published installed price does not answer all three. These are attributed budget observations, not live quotes or a national average.

Material-only price gap: this review did not verify a current, new first-quality NZ retail panel price with a matching product, unit, GST basis and coverage. The worksheet therefore starts with no price. Enter a real supplier quote to calculate a panel subtotal. Do not subtract an assumed labour rate from these guides to invent a supply price.

blocks.title: Why there is no single “cheapest roof” verdict

blocks.text: Roofing Systems lists metal tiles and long-run at the same installed budgeting figure. Arcline’s 2024 guide gives different figures and leaves some scope questions open; Delta’s 2025 figures include roof replacement work. That is evidence of differing scopes and assumptions, not a reliable national ranking. Ask suppliers to price the same roof, finish and inclusions.

The NZMRM code describes manufacturer-appointed, trained installers and notes that tiles are not normally supplied to other installers. That helps explain the lack of retail panel prices, but does not establish any particular supplier margin.

sections.title: How many metal roof panels do I need?

blocks.text: Use the actual sloping roof area and the published panel density for the selected profile. A panel contains several visual tile shapes, so counting those shapes is not the same as ordering panels. Rounded cover-area figures are not used to recalculate the manufacturer’s stated density.

blocks.title: What this worksheet can and cannot tell you

blocks.text: RoofHub calculates planning quantities from your inputs. It does not lay out individual roof faces or optimise cut panels, hips, valleys and short courses. Confirm the order with the installer’s panel schedule. An allowance is your assumption, not a manufacturer-approved waste percentage.

A panel price only prices the panels. A separate batten worksheet, when enabled, divides area by an installer-provided gauge as a rough quantity check. It does not select a batten size, fixing, support span or installation design.

sections.title: What does metal tile look like on a new home?

blocks.text: These builder and manufacturer accounts show metal tiles used in new-home specifications and residential designs, rather than treating the product only as an old roof to remove. They are not a survey of market share, and we have not inspected the homes. No separate roofing invoice is published for these examples.

Compare the same roof, not different house prices

sections.title: Which modern metal-tile profile should I compare?

blocks.text: Gerard’s current NZ site says Metrotile is now Gerard. Older project pages and quotes can retain former brand and profile names. Do not count nine profiles from the same product family as nine independent manufacturers, or assume an old profile name is an exact match for a current replacement.

blocks.title: Satin, stone-chip and concealed fixing are different decisions

blocks.text: Satin describes a smooth finish and textured describes a stone-coated finish. Bond and Classic publish both finish types. Concealed fastening describes the fixing arrangement, not a guarantee that all such panels share the same cover or support design. Compare a physical colour sample and the exact panel specification.

Do not compare a tile’s decorative coating thickness or finished weight directly with a long-run sheet’s base metal thickness. Calibre, for example, describes a 0.55 mm steel core, but that does not make every tile a 0.55 mm product or prove a generic strength ranking.

sections.title: What should a complete new-roof quote include?

blocks.text: Conventional metal tiles and concealed-fix systems do not all use the same support assembly. The conventional Gerard appraisal describes tiles and flashings above roofing underlay and battens. The CF appraisal describes plywood sheathing, with a batten alternative identified for CF Shake, CF Shingle and CF Slate. Confirm Calibre’s support specification separately.

blocks.caption: A quote scope checklist, not a priced bill of materials

cells: Profile, finish, covered quantity, cuts, spares and whether the price is per panel, pack or m².
Specified product, coverage including laps, support requirements and installation responsibility.
Which support system, timber/decking supply and labour, plus any strengthening or extra supports.
The matching trim type, measured lengths and overlaps. Do not reuse a long-run ridge price for a tile accessory.
Valley material, supporting work, apron details and flashing around every pipe or skylight.
System-approved fixings, vents and any selected solar-mounting details.
Delivery, safe access, waste handling, GST, installation warranty and the exclusions schedule.

blocks.text: Avoid counting underlay labour twice. Ask whether the installer’s tile rate already includes underlay and batten installation; keep the cost of supplying those materials separate. The panel worksheet does not add installation labour.

blocks.title: Support checks matter more than a low panel price

blocks.text: Do not treat one generic batten spacing as an installation instruction. Layout, attachments, loads and perimeter details must follow the selected system. Nor should the area-based panel total be treated as proof of weather resistance or structural compliance.

sections.title: Panel quantities for 100, 150, 200 and 250 m² roofs

blocks.text: To turn this into a panel-only budget, multiply the purchase quantity by a genuine per-panel quote and keep its GST convention visible. Pack rounding and minimum quantities can change the purchased amount. None of these counts includes trims, fixings, underlay, supports, labour, delivery or removal.

blocks.text: The product minima in this comparison range from 10° for Calibre to 12° for Bond, Classic and Milano, and 15° for Shake, Senator and the other CF profiles shown. They are product-specific starting points, not permission to use every metal tile at 10°.

blocks.title: Conditions to take to your designer or installer

blocks.text: The appraisal scope includes limits on geometry, wind exposure, supporting construction and pitch. Long roof runs can introduce additional pitch requirements. Use the full current appraisal and installation manual for the selected roof; a short product table cannot replace those conditions.
Roof pitch means the roof structure’s slope, not the local angle of one stepped panel surface. Measure it from plans or a safe location; there is no need to climb onto the roof to use these tools.

blocks.text: Check plan area versus actual roof area before multiplying quantities. A two-storey home’s total floor area is not its roof footprint.
